words.headline: Brrr-ooklyn and Beyond: No-Heat Calls Hit Four Times the Usual
words.blurb: With a high of just 48 degrees, New Yorkers filed 3,269 no-heat requests, more than four times the typical 734. A light 0.14 inches of rain also nudged sewer problems up to 250, nearly triple the norm.

boroughs.Bronx: The Bronx led the city's chill with 1,086 no-heat requests, its top mood by far.
boroughs.Brooklyn: Brooklyn still found time for parking wars (988), just edging out no heat (934).
boroughs.Manhattan: Manhattan reached for the sweaters: no heat topped the list with 793 requests.
boroughs.Queens: Queens kept its eyes on the curb, with parking wars on top at 766.
boroughs.Staten Island: Staten Island split between parking wars (77) and rainy water and sewer woes (76).

rare_finds.name: Hotel or motel: bookings under 4 hours accepted
rare_finds.quip: Someone at City Hall sat down and decided four hours is the line. Not three. Not five. Four. Who did the math on that?

rare_finds.name: Locksmith: demand for cash payment
rare_finds.quip: You're locked out, cold, holding a card, and the one person with the key wants paper money. There's a form for that. Of course there is.

rare_finds.name: Employment agency: advertising false or misleading
rare_finds.quip: What's the deal with an agency whose whole job is finding jobs needing a complaint category? Somebody had to get hired to write it.
